title: Vision UX Analysis Contract (Qualitative, No Scoring)
description: Contract for modules/analysis's first prototype, implemented in 11_Benchmark_Engine/modules/analysis/. Distinct from analysis.schema.json: that contract is reserved for the future SCORED AnalysisOutput (journey_scores, innovation_scores, ai_maturity_level, mandatory_questions). This contract is a single-homepage, qualitative, non-comparative UX read — a screenshot plus a Discovery Report go in, a structured but unscored analysis comes out. No scoring, no cross-company comparison, no benchmark verdict. Sprint 6 wires the interface and data flow only; the model call itself (modules/analysis/visionModelClient.js) is a stub until a later sprint connects a real vision-capable model (e.g. GPT-5 Vision).

VisionUXAnalysisInput.description: Everything the analyzer needs: one screenshot, one Discovery Report. Nothing else — no other screenshots, no other companies, no prior benchmark state.

screenshot_path.description: Path to a single homepage screenshot, as produced by modules/vision/screenshotRunner.js.

discovery_report.description: Consumed directly as Discovery's output type — no separate transport format, same pattern analysis.schema.json already uses for vision_output.

model.description: Name/version of the vision model that produced this — recorded for provenance once a real call is wired in.

Findings.description: Every field is a short, evidence-grounded paragraph describing what is visible in the screenshot — no numeric score, no rating, no comparison to any other product.

first_impression.description: What a first-time visitor would register in the first few seconds.

visual_hierarchy.description: What draws the eye first, second, third, and whether that order matches likely user intent.

main_cta_effectiveness.description: Whether the primary call-to-action is identifiable, prominent, and unambiguous.

navigation_clarity.description: Whether a visitor could tell where to go next, independent of Discovery's structural nav findings.

ai_feature_visibility.description: Whether any AI capability is visually evident on the homepage itself, not just present in copy/markup (cross-checked against discovery_report.detected_ai_capabilities).

information_density.description: Whether the page feels sparse, balanced, or overloaded.

trust_signals.description: Visible credibility markers: reviews, press mentions, security badges, familiar brand patterns — or their absence.

accessibility_observations.description: Visually apparent accessibility concerns: contrast, text size, reliance on color alone, crowded tap targets. Not a WCAG audit.
